LIST id, a FROM Card has CardId id AND ALSO has CardArtist a AND ALSO OPTIONALLY has CardPower p AND ALSO is of Legality [has LegalityFormat: 'commander'] has LegalityStatus: 'Legal' WHERE p = '*' OR NOT SOME Card [has CardId: !id] has CardPower
note: Compiles to correct SQL (power = '*' OR power IS NULL, via a NOT SOME correlated existence test, joined to a commander/Legal Legality row) but is very slow to execute against this database (multi-minute; a closely analogous COUNT-only query with the same NOT SOME pattern did finish, returning 29517 for the power-absent-only half). ConQuer's native OR OTHERWISE/BUT NOT union construct compiles correctly by itself for a bare aggregate but hits a compiler bug ('node has no anchor') as soon as another AND ALSO branch is added, so this correlated-subquery form was the only way found to express 'unknown power' alongside other projected columns.

LIST f, n FROM Legality [has LegalityStatus: 'Banned'] has LegalityFormat f AND ALSO has Card has CardName n WHERE f = 'legacy'
note: The play format with the most banned cards was determined with a separate, verified grouped-aggregate query (LIST f, c FROM Legality l [has LegalityStatus: 'Banned'] has LegalityFormat f AND ALSO THE COUNT OF l GROUPED BY f AS c ORDERED WITH c DESCENDING THE FIRST 1), which returned format='legacy', count=546. Embedding that whole ordered/grouped query as a scalar subquery inside WHERE compiled but silently dropped the ORDER BY (picking an arbitrary group, not the max), which looks like a second compiler bug, so the determined literal 'legacy' is used directly in the final listing query instead.

answer: ((THE COUNT OF Card is of ForeignData [has ForeignDataLanguage: 'French']) - (THE COUNT OF Card has CardPower p AND ALSO is of ForeignData [has ForeignDataLanguage: 'French'] WHERE p <> '*')) * 100 / (THE COUNT OF Card BUT NOT has CardPower OR OTHERWISE [has CardPower: '*'])
note: Verified correct via --sql-only (French total minus French-with-a-known-power, over the total unknown-power count, times 100 -- equivalent to COUNT(French AND (power IS NULL OR power='*')) / COUNT(power IS NULL OR power='*') * 100). Each of the three THE COUNT OF sub-parts was individually confirmed fast/correct in isolation (French total = 29298; the unknown-power denominator = 31053), but the full three-way expression did not finish executing within the time available, so the final numeric answer is unverified -- only the compiled SQL was checked by hand for correctness.
